idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with visible project activity and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • See files, commands, tests and relationships in the Activity Map.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Your conversation is never written to disk.

Sightline is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, JetBrains or Google. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "Android Studio" is a trademark of Google. Both are used only to describe compatibility.

Copyright © 2026 Michael Carroll. Source-available — the source is published so it can be read and audited, but it is not open source and may not be redistributed. Using Sightline in your work, including commercially, is expressly permitted. Free during the beta. See the licence accompanying this listing.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.0

  • Switch models from the composer. The / actions menu has a new Model submenu — the CLI's aliases (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable), any full model id you pin, and a line reporting what the CLI says it is actually running. Switching mid-conversation takes effect in place, keeping the session and the conversation.
  • Wide tables render again. A Markdown table whose cells were wider than the chat column showed as an empty bordered box; it now scrolls horizontally instead.
  • Light-theme fix for the Agent Activity Map. Its toolbar and activity-log bar rendered as dark strips around a correctly light graph, because the chrome and the graph were deriving their background differently. The map now paints as a single surface.

0.5.0 — first stable release. Same build as 0.5.0-beta, promoted after a hands-on pass over the interactive approval and diff paths. Everything below shipped during the beta.

0.5.0-beta

  • Now requires Android Studio Quail 2 (2026.1.2) or later. The previous compatibility floor was the 2025.3 platform, kept for reach — but that older platform lacks API the current one requires, which left Sightline calling methods Android Studio has since deprecated. Supporting the current platform properly is worth more than claiming an older one. IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1+ is the same platform build and can still install it.
  • No deprecated platform API remains in the plugin, and the pre-release verification now runs against Android Studio at that floor rather than against IntelliJ IDEA.

0.4.0-beta

  • A message you send while Claude is working now reaches the work in progress. Pressing Enter mid-turn used to park the message until the turn was over — by which time the agent had usually finished going the way you were trying to redirect it. It is now delivered into the running session and folded into the current turn at the agent's next step, so "also update the tests" or "stop, wrong file" arrives while it still matters. The message is marked Sent while Claude was working, and what the agent says next appears below it, so the transcript still reads in the order things happened.
  • Queuing remains for the one case where nothing can receive a message — a Stop in flight, or a session that has exited — and those messages still go out with the next turn. If the session ends in the instant between the check and the send, your text stays in the composer and you're told, rather than a message that looks sent reaching nobody.

0.3.1-beta

  • Compatibility fix: installs on Android Studio 2026.1 (build 261) and later again — a stray upper build-limit in the previous artifact's descriptor has been removed.

0.3.0-beta

  • Generate commit messages. A new button in the commit dialog's message toolbar reads the diff of the changes you're committing and drafts a message into the field — using a fast, low-effort model by default. It follows a commit style your project already states (a "Commit messages" section in CONTRIBUTING, a .gitmessage template, a commitlint config, or CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md), and disables while it drafts. The model and optional style guidance are configurable in Settings → Tools → Sightline.

0.2.0-beta

  • Mermaid diagrams render natively. ```mermaid flowcharts and state diagrams draw as real diagrams in the transcript — shapes for decisions and states, directional edges, start/final markers — with a Source toggle and Copy. Other diagram types fall back to a code block. Claude is told the panel supports them, so it reaches for a diagram where one illustrates better.
  • A clearer, calmer Activity Map. A mode picker (Everything, Changes, Problems, Data flow, Navigation, Test coverage) selects the nodes and edges that matter; nodes are drawn by type as distinct shapes (files, commands, tests, warnings, errors) so the graph reads without relying on colour; edges carry direction arrows; and a compact legend key sits in the corner.
  • Trustworthy run status. A single recovered command failure no longer turns the whole run red while work continues — it's shown as a separate health note. Each turn ends with a structured completion card (Completed / Completed with warnings / Stopped) and any observed warnings, instead of one grey line.
  • Better composer. A message queued behind a running turn is an editable card (Edit / Cancel), not an easy-to-miss count; and the composer collapses to a single row while Claude works, restoring the moment you click it.

Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta gains all of the above. Still a beta — please report problems on the public issue tracker.
